chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar said, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Khattab and Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, on the authority of Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, on the authority of who he mentioned, on the authority of Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, on the authority of Abu Abdillah, on the authority of his forefathers (AS)

He said: The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) said: 'Whoever Allah promises to reward for an action, He will fulfill it for him. And whoever He threatens with punishment for an action, He is in it with the choice (to punish or pardon).'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Allah's promise and threat in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the theological distinction between Allah's promise (wa'd) and threat (wa'd), establishing that divine promises of reward are absolute and binding, while threats of punishment remain discretionary, allowing for divine mercy or pardon. This principle underscores the Shia understanding of divine justice balanced with grace, where human free will interacts with God's ultimate authority to forgive. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the nature of divine attributes in al-Saduq's al-Tawhid.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan alSaffar said, on the authority of both Muhammad ibn Abu al-Khattab and Ahmad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Barqi, on the authority of `Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, on the authority of who he mentioned, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja`fari on the authority of Abu `Abd Allah (AS), on the authority of his forefathers (AS)

that The Messenger of Allah (SA) said: “Whoever Allah promises to reward for an action, He will fulfill it. And whoever He threatens with punishment over an action, He may choose (either punishment or pardon).”
